mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS signals accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS declines or Rank IC <0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in UNRATE above 5% indicates labor market stress, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, which may drive negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly negative when UNRATE crosses above 5%, or p-value >0.05 in t-test.

mechanism_narrative: High demand growth (GDPC1) coupled with accommodative monetary policy (low FEDFUNDS) creates a virtuous cycle, lifting equity valuations and generating positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not significantly positive despite high GDPC1 and low FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC <0.03 over 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong supply growth (INDPRO) alongside cooling inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests sustainable economic expansion without overheating, supporting equity valuations and positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive when INDPRO rises and CPIAUCSL falls, or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion with sub-2% CPIAUCSL, persistent FEDFUNDS easing (low rates) signals accommodative policy, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive despite FEDFUNDS easing in the regime, or p-value >0.05 in t-test.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in demand growth (GDPC1) above 12,000 billion chained dollars indicates accommodated consumption, prompting positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not significantly positive when GDPC1 crosses above 12,000, or Rank IC <0.03 over 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of rising supply growth (INDPRO) and falling unemployment (UNRATE <4%) reflects robust economic momentum, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive when INDPRO rises and UNRATE falls, or p-value >0.05 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market with UNRATE below 3% and rising employment (PAYEMS), strong labor demand signals economic strength, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive when UNRATE <3% and PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC <0.03 over 2-year window.
